title: Optional auto-scroll that any user input hands back
summary: An `aria-pressed` Auto toggle, off on every visit, advances Lenis by `90 px × dt` on the shared ticker (`lenis.scrollTo(y, { immediate: true })` from a float accumulator, `dt` clamped to `100 ms`); a capture-phase wheel, touchstart, pointerdown or keydown anywhere but the toggle hands control back at once, as does any scroll more than `3 px` from where it was written (scrollbar, find-in-page, a link) and reaching the end; each change written once to a polite `role="status"` line; under reduced motion and static the toggle stays focusable but `aria-disabled`, with the reason in its description
variants: fixed 90 px/s on a reading page, stops at the end (this, default)
film clock: drive a speed-capped progress clock instead of the document, the same hand-back on input (see gl-progress-scene-windows)
resume after idle: offer, never start, a Resume button a few seconds after a hand-back
